payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show the woman wearing or otherwise visibly having a helmet on her head?
node.criteria: Pass if a helmet is visibly on the woman’s head; fail if the image clearly shows that she does not have a helmet on her head; unknown if the woman, her head, or the presence of a helmet cannot be determined.
node.binding: The woman in the input image; the requested result is a helmet visibly on her head.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image clearly shows the woman wearing a helmet on her head.

fulfillment: The node is already performing well: the edited image visibly shows a helmet on the woman’s head, and both endpoint and source-comparison traces support completion with high confidence; aggregate agreement and coverage are 1.0. No semantic change is indicated. For future robustness, preserve the distinction between endpoint evidence that establishes fulfillment and comparison evidence that only supports whether the requested change was added; do not require both checks when endpoint evidence is clear. The abbreviated binding should retain an unambiguous reference to the woman in the source image, but this case shows no binding failure.
s2: The node passes this case: the edited image visibly adds a helmet to the woman, and the source comparison confirms it was absent before; the high-confidence traces and aggregate agreement/coverage support the reference. No semantic change is indicated. For robustness, keep the binding explicit about the woman in the source image and distinguish endpoint evidence of fulfillment from comparison evidence of an edit. Do not make comparison a mandatory dependency when endpoint evidence already establishes fulfillment. The abbreviated binding in the supplied variable is ambiguous, so ensure typed edits preserve the full target and requested-change meaning; do not infer a failure from that abbreviation alone.

Treat uncertainty as unresolved rather than as evidence of absence."}
